incident.title: [DEMO C039] A Sheets action is missing after catalog discovery
incident.description: The agent is missing a required Sheets action after catalog discovery, despite it appearing in the current catalog; a provider outage may be involved.

tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.

What canonical records cover the 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z window for Sheets catalog discovery in tool-executor with null filters first: discovery request/response logs, returned action counts/items, any truncation/pagination fields, latency/error rate, backlog, and affected-tenant identifiers? We need exact records showing whether the missing Sheets action was absent from the discovery response at incident time versus only absent later in the agent view.

Were there any concurrent changes or external dependency issues in the same window affecting catalog/discovery inputs: tool-executor deploys/config changes, toolkit/version pin changes, Sheets provider catalog updates, auth/permission surface changes, or provider status events? Please gather timestamps and compare them against first-failure timing rather than treating temporal overlap as proof.

Which hypothesis best matches the observed failed execution path for the affected tenant: tool discovery truncation/pagination, connection/auth surface isolation, tenant-specific permissions/configuration, provider failure, or an internal regression? What discriminating control exists—such as another tenant or request in the same window, a controlled discovery with different limits/version, or logs showing the request never reached the provider—to separate these causes?
Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
Write the evidence-backed internal report and proposed next steps.

objections: Do not treat ev_64d21291b27a / sheets-discovery-039:dependencies:0 as contradicting truncation; provider reachability is only counter-evidence to the outage theory, not to the observed first-page omission.

Keep the causal claim scoped: the evidence supports an incident-time discovery truncation / incomplete pagination outcome for cedar's observed request, but not a proven explanation for all 380 blocked operations in the window.

notes: Canonical incident-time discovery record for tool-executor is ev_1b8d7225c1b0 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0 (also returned by ev_116aabfa38ba / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0 and ev_f9b9f15dfce6 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0): 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z, tenant cedar, request_id req-39, toolkit googlesheets, status 200, list_limit 20, returned_tools 20, has_more true, requested_tool_on_later_page true, version_contains_tool true. This shows the requested Sheets action was not on the first discovery page at incident time, while the catalog version did contain it.

Comparison and impact records: ev_fa5228b7ff1d / sheets-discovery-039:metrics:0 shows cedar at 10:05 with 602 requests, 0 failures, 380 business_operations_blocked, queue_depth 108, p95_latency_ms 1440; ev_fa5228b7ff1d / sheets-discovery-039:metrics:1 shows maple with 516 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked, queue_depth 0, p95_latency_ms 160. ev_1b8d7225c1b0 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:1 shows maple had status 200 and unrelated same-provider reads succeeding, which is counter-evidence to a broad provider outage.

Dependency/deployment context is limited: ev_64d21291b27a / sheets-discovery-039:dependencies:0 says tool-executor depends on auth-service, provider-api, session-policy and provider_api_reachable=true; ev_240f301d9d71 / sheets-discovery-039:deployments:0 is an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05. These do not show a tool-executor outage or relevant deployment in the window.

Important gap: supplied canonical logs do not include a full discovery response body, action-item list, page token, or subsequent pagination requests/responses for cedar within 09:50–10:15. So the observed evidence supports 'absent from the first returned page at incident time' but does not by itself prove whether the agent later failed to paginate, filtered the result, or dropped the action after discovery.

First observed incident-time failure signal is the cedar discovery request at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z: tool-executor returned 20 tools with has_more=true, and the requested Sheets action was on a later page even though it existed in the catalog version seen by that request (ev_1b8d7225c1b0 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0).

No concurrent tool-executor deploy/config change is evidenced in the supplied records. The only deployment in the window is an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05:00Z, temporally overlapping but on another service, so it is not proof of impact on discovery inputs (ev_240f301d9d71 / sheets-discovery-039:deployments:0). A time-bounded dependency query for tool-executor returned no additional change records, which is a telemetry gap for config/pin history rather than proof none occurred (ev_589a17b60e5e).

External dependency outage evidence is weak: tool-executor reported provider_api_reachable=true, and at the same 10:05:00Z timestamp another tenant (maple) had status 200 with same provider available and an unrelated Sheets read succeeding, which counters a broad Sheets/provider status event or auth-surface outage affecting all tenants (ev_64d21291b27a / sheets-discovery-039:dependencies:0; ev_1b8d7225c1b0 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:1).

Observed impact is tenant-specific rather than platform-wide at 10:05:00Z: cedar had 602 requests, 0 failures, but 380 business operations blocked, queue_depth 108, p95 latency 1440 ms, while maple had 516 requests, 0 blocked ops, queue_depth 0, p95 160 ms (ev_fa5228b7ff1d / sheets-discovery-039:metrics:0; ev_fa5228b7ff1d / sheets-discovery-039:metrics:1). The supplied evidence does not include canonical records for toolkit/version pin changes, Sheets provider catalog updates, or auth/permission changes in this window.

hypothesis.description: The failed cedar execution most likely came from incomplete Sheets tool discovery: the incident-time discovery response stopped at the first 20 tools even though more pages existed, and the needed Sheets action was on a later page in the same catalog version.
assumptions: This explains the observed missing action during discovery for cedar, not necessarily every blocked operation in the window.

The supplied logs prove the tool was absent from the first returned page at incident time, but do not fully show whether later pagination was never attempted, was filtered, or was dropped after discovery.

The controlled sandbox comparison changes only sheets_configuration, so it is discriminating for the stated discovery behavior but not proof of the exact production code path or root configuration source.

findings.statement: At incident time, cedar's googlesheets discovery returned status 200 with list_limit=20, returned_tools=20, has_more=true, and the requested tool flagged as being on a later page while the version still contained that tool.
In the controlled sandbox, the original condition reproduced the same truncation pattern, while the corrected condition completed pagination and found the requested Sheets tool.

Impact was concentrated in cedar: 602 requests, 0 transport failures, but 380 business operations blocked, queue_depth 108, p95 latency 1440 ms; comparison tenant maple had 516 requests, 0 blocked operations, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms.
A same-window comparison tenant had status 200, same provider available, and an unrelated Sheets read succeeding, which separates the cedar failure from a broad provider outage.
